root_idea.summary: The root centers on expansive, unrestricted eating in conditions of abundance and fertility, especially grazing and consuming what one wishes.
root_idea.development: The core sense of abundant feeding develops into animal pasturing, human indulgence, places and states of plenty, and derived expressions for causing or finding abundant pasture.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The supplied Quranic group is a distinct Form I verb; its inflected QAC lemma is normalized to the classical perfect citation form رَتَعَ.

senses.definition: To feed, graze, or eat and drink freely and abundantly.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the verb has a human subject and may express abundant eating metaphorically, extending the basic image of an animal feeding freely amid plenty.

senses.definition: To enjoy oneself, amuse oneself, or move about freely and cheerfully.
senses.usage_conditions: In يوسف 12:12, this interpretation occurs in the construction يَرْتَعْ وَيَلْعَبْ, where the verb expresses enjoyment or carefree activity alongside play.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To indulge freely in eating and drinking from another person's property, acting without restraint in such consumption.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction with بِفِي مَالِ or equivalent wording, distinct from ordinary grazing or feeding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Figuratively, to go about or enter a place freely, as though taking unrestricted nourishment from pasture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in idiomatic expressions for approaching a prohibited pasture and for entering a spiritually nourishing gathering by analogy with grazing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put camels or other animals to pasture, leaving them to eat and drink at will.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This Form IV entry is also associated with an alternative reading discussed for the Yusuf passage; no separate Form IV QAC form group is supplied in the packet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To govern or manage subjects well, as though leaving them free to satisfy themselves in pasture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of putting animals to pasture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a group of people, to come upon abundant herbage and pasture there.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a party that encounters plentiful grazing and pastures.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To produce abundant herbage, or, of land, to become rich in herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The producing sense is used of rain; the becoming-abundant sense is used of land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A plentiful, pleasant, and easy life.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun denoting a condition of material ease and abundance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Abundance of herbage or of life's goods, conveniences, and comforts; a state of ampleness and plenty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may denote either fertile pasture or general material prosperity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who continually seeks successive places of pasture abundant in herbage for his camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An occupational or habitual description of a person moving between fertile grazing places.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel or other beast pasturing at will and eating and drinking freely amid abundant herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The participle is also applied in the plural to a people or group in قَوْمٌ رَاتِعُونَ.
A plural nominal usage distinct from the pasture-related meanings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of pasturing, or pasture itself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place where animals graze and consume what they wish amid abundance; the noun can also denote the pasture of a land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who leaves travelling camels to pasture at will, allowing them to eat and drink freely in abundant grazing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV active participle describing the person responsible for leaving the animals to pasture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having or characterized by abundant herbage, goods, conveniences, or comforts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person, a people, or herbage when abundance is habitual or prevalent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of rain, producing or giving growth to abundant herbage suitable for grazing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A participial description of rain by its effect on pasture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of land, providing grazing in which animals eagerly seek to satiate themselves.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes land attractive to animals because of its plentiful herbage.

cautions: The supplied QAC occurrence is the Form I imperfect يَرْتَعْ. The evidence also preserves a Form IV reading يُرْتِعْ associated with the Yusuf passage, but no separate QAC Form IV group is supplied; it is therefore retained under its own normalized headword أَرْتَعَ rather than merged into the Form I entry.
The Yusuf occurrence supports both an abundant-feeding interpretation and an enjoyment or carefree-activity interpretation; the supplied contextual gloss reflects the latter.
